label: Chainlink CCIP requirements
summary: Atomic EVM-only requirements for one directional CCIP lane. Select it through --chainlink-product ccip; this definition is not deployment or provider-support evidence.
requiredFacts: One source-to-destination EVM lane with distinct EIP-155 chain IDs and uint64 Chainlink chain selectors; a reverse lane is a separate profile
Exact router, sender and receiver roles, addresses, runtime-code hashes, dependency lock, payload schema and application domain
Source inclusion, destination execution, finality, rate-limit and fee-funding policies
Replay, duplicate, out-of-order, bounded-pending-work and terminal-recovery behavior with a pre-bound beneficiary
Send and receive execution outside PoolManager callbacks
requiredFiles: Content-addressed EVM-only Chainlink provider profile selecting CCIP
Source and destination deployment evidence with runtime-code hashes and dependency lock
Directional sender and receiver source plus payload schema
Finality, rate-limit, fee-funding and terminal-recovery policies
requiredTests: Wrong source or destination chain, selector, router, sender, receiver, runtime hash, application domain and payload schema
Replay, duplicate, reordering, partial delivery, reorg and destination execution failure
Fee exhaustion, rate limiting, outage, timeout and permissionless terminal recovery
Bounded payload size, pending messages, retries and total completion work
No CCIP send or receive execution inside a PoolManager callback
risks: Chain IDs and Chainlink selectors are different domains and can be confused
A valid source message can execute in the wrong application lane without exact domain binding
Unbounded pending work or privileged recovery can trap or redirect user value
A structural plan can be mistaken for deployed router or provider availability evidence
